extracted.intended_audience: Early-career physician-scientists applying for NIH K08 career development awards (and their mentors/institutional research administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and critique-level review criteria used by an NIH study section to evaluate a Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award (K08). Includes the scored Overall Impact and detailed criterion-based evaluation (Candidate, Career Development, Research Plan, Mentors, Environment) plus human subjects/administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: assigned an overall impact/priority score (example here: 17). The Impact/Priority score reflects the likelihood the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after committee discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by individual assigned reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. The Resume and Summary of Discussion section summarizes the final opinion of the committee after discussion and is the basis for the assigned Impact/Priority score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate (qualifications and productivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the applicant's training, qualifications, prior productivity, and potential to become an independent investigator (e.g., MD/PhD training, fellowship, publications, prior T32 support, global health experience, letters of reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note strengths such as excellent training in microbial pathogenesis, strong productivity including first-author publications (including recent Cell paper), relevant clinical/global experience, and laudatory reference letters. Weaknesses would be noted if absent. Reviewers weigh candidate's background relative to proposed career trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals / Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the quality, specificity, and adequacy of the career development plan and mentoring strategy to prepare the candidate for an independent research career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include clear long-term goals and planned activities. Weaknesses include lack of a formal career development plan, no plans for formal coursework in critical specialty areas (host-microbial interactions, host immunity, biostatistics), and insufficient detail on how the K08 will strengthen expertise. Reviewers expect concrete coursework/training and defined mentoring/monitoring plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan (significance, innovation, approach, preliminary data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the conceptual framework, specific aims, preliminary data, rigor and feasibility of the experimental approach, and integration of aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers value a well-rationalized, integrated set of aims supported by strong preliminary data. Strengths cited: novel focus (antigen-specific Ab Fc-mediated mechanisms), supportive preliminary serum and in vitro macrophage data, logical progression of aims (define Ag specificity; dissect Fc/FcR mediated restriction; identify macrophage effector mechanisms). Weaknesses cited: lack of clarity how latent disease patients will be identified, lack of strategy to prioritize among many possible antigen reactivities, apparent non-specific protection seen in controls, and limited linkage between insights from Aim 1 to Aims 2 and 3. Reviewers expect experimental controls, validation cohorts, clear patient definitions, and plans to translate findings between aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentors, Co-Mentors, Consultants, Collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the mentoring team’s expertise, complementary skills, commitment, and the advisory committee structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong mentorship is evidenced by complementary senior investigators (e.g., experts in TB heterogeneity, antibody/Fc profiling), an advisory committee with relevant expertise (inflammasome, FcR function, cell biology, microbiology), letters describing active monitoring and mentorship plans, and access to clinical samples/statistical support. Reviewers mark absence of mentoring support as a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of institutional resources, protected time, laboratory space, and explicit institutional support for the candidate's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include a committed letter guaranteeing 75% protected research time, limiting clinical duties to 10%, guaranteed space and K08 resources, access to state-of-the-art profiling and imaging, and a strong local TB research community. Reviewers look for documented institutional commitment and infrastructure to support the research and training plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of protections for human subjects, informed consent plans, and compliance with NIH human subjects policies. (Example code: '30 ACCEPTABLE')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study enrolls adults aged 18-75 with latent or active TB able to give informed consent; study sites and cohorts are described. Projects must conform to NIH policies on protection of human subjects; guidance and links provided. Reviewers check for appropriate consent, vulnerable population considerations, sample provenance, and whether FOIA/PII/confidentiality concerns are addressed. Example comment: 'Most or all biological specimens will come from established specimen repositories.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to monitor participant safety and data integrity for studies involving human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'ACCEPTABLE' for this application. Reviewers expect an appropriate DSM plan consistent with study risk; details depend on study type and funding level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to include eligible women in study populations and comply with NIH inclusion policies. (Example code: 'G1A ACCEPTABLE')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible adult males and females from all ethnic backgrounds are included in the cohorts. Projects must conform to NIH policies on inclusion of women; details of population and inclusion/exclusion rationale must be provided to the NIH program administrator prior to undertaking the studies. Reviewers expect justification if women are excluded or underrepresented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Minorities Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to include racial and ethnic minority populations consistent with NIH policies. (Example code: 'M1A ACCEPTABLE')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible adult males and females from all ethnic backgrounds are included; because TB disproportionately affects underrepresented groups, such samples are expected to be well represented. Reviewers expect explanation of inclusion/exclusion criteria and rationale; program administrator must receive details prior to studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether children are included or excluded and compliance with NIH policies concerning pediatric inclusion. (Example code: 'C3A ACCEPTABLE')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application includes no children. If children will be included in supported projects, investigators must conform to NIH policies and provide rationale and protections. Reviewers confirm appropriateness of exclusion/inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether vertebrate animals are used and compliance with animal welfare policies. (Example code: '10 NOT APPLICABLE')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No live vertebrate animals are involved in this competing application. If vertebrate animals are used, reviewers check that appropriate protocols and justifications are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazard Comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of biohazard identification and appropriateness of handling procedures and containment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'ACCEPTABLE' for this application. Comments noted access to BSL-3 space at the Ragon Institute and Harvard School of Public Health, demonstrated procedures for working with mycobacteria, and no concerns. Reviewers expect explicit biosafety plans and facilities documentation where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of planned RCR training format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, and frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'ACCEPTABLE'. Format: experiential, didactic and seminar based. Subject matter: research ethics, regulatory requirements, subject privacy and other key areas. Faculty participation: full participation of mentorship committee. Duration: initial coursework involving 16 hours of face time. Frequency: biannual discussions with advisory committee. Reviewers expect a clear RCR curriculum and monitoring plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (Data, Model Organisms, Genomic Data Sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for sharing data, model organisms, and genomic data consistent with NIH and institutional guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'ACCEPTABLE' and 'Consistent with NIH and institutional guidelines'. If budget exceeds thresholds (e.g., >$500,000/year), additional Data Sharing Plan comments may apply. Reviewers expect concrete sharing models and compliance with GDS policy when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to authenticate biological reagents and resources to ensure reproducibility and validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'ACCEPTABLE'. Reviewers look for documentation that biological resources are appropriately authenticated and provenance described (e.g., established specimen repositories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the requested budget and project period are reasonable and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The budget was recommended as requested in this case. Administrative note: the budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect any reviewer recommendations; if an award is planned, grants management staff will calculate costs based on committee budget recommendations. Reviewers expect justified budgets aligned with scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Significance / Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the project's potential impact on public health and the field (e.g., one-third world burden of TB; potential to inform diagnostics, vaccines, therapeutics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Narrative should state public health relevance; reviewers consider whether the research addresses important problems and has potential to generate biomarkers, diagnostics, or vaccine strategies. Strength: novel focus on humoral immunity in TB may inform diagnostics and rational vaccine design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Critique Format (Strengths and Weaknesses per Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Format used by reviewers to communicate detailed strengths and weaknesses across core review criteria (Candidate; Career Development; Research Plan; Mentors; Environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique sections include enumerated strengths and weaknesses with examples from the application (e.g., specific missing coursework, unclear patient definitions, strong preliminary data). These comments are provided without significant modification by staff to indicate the range of committee comments and may not reflect the final outcome; the Resume and Summary of Discussion summarizes the committee's final opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects / Animal Subjects Status Codes and Labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of coded status labels to summarize compliance and involvement (examples in this document: 'Human Subjects: 30 - Human subjects involved - Certified, no SRG concerns'; 'Animal Subjects: 10 - No live vertebrate animals involved').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and staff use codes to indicate acceptability or applicability. These codes link to required documentation and policies. Applicants should ensure supporting documentation corresponds to the labeled status.
